newsitem.title: FRANCE: Maize yields at record high in France's southwest.
newsitem.headline: Maize yields at record high in France's southwest.

text.p: With the maize harvest drawing to an end in France local crop analysts have revised yield estimates sharply upwards in the southwest and downwards in the east.
In the Aquitaine region, where most of France's maize is produced the harvest is now 75-80 percent complete.
Heavy rainfall slowed combining last week but the harvest may to be over by the end of the month, analysts said.
Local ONIC officials said they had sharply raised their estimates for 1996 maize yields to a record 9.3-9.4 tonnes per hectare from a pre-harvest target of 8.6 tonnes per hectare.
This would represent a strong jump from a yield of 8.0 tonnes last year.
"This is an excellent surprise," said one analyst, who linked the upwards revision to the stronger-than-expected performance of non-irrigated maize.
Non-irrigated patches benefited from good moisture levels throughout the autumn, he said.
Regional area is also expected to rise by 4.2 percent to 370,000 hectares.
Local ONIC officials said that assuming higher yields and area, the delivered crop may jump by some 30 percent to 2.9 million tonnes.
In eastern France the harvest is now 80-85 percent complete and local analysts said they had again revised downwards yield estimates.
They explained the maize suffered from dry conditions in the summer while cool temperatures slowed down plant development in autumn.
Analysts are now forecasting yields of 9.0 tonnes per hectare down from the 9.2 tonnes they predicted two weeks ago. This would compare with 8.9 tonnes last year.
Delivered crop may reach 1.1 million tonnes, up 12 percent over last year, mostly due to a rise in area.
Regional area is expected to rise to 126,00 hectares from 115,000 hectares.
The region is the third maize producer after the Aquitaine and Midi-Pyrenees regions.
On Friday the French farm ministry raised its estimate for the national 1996 maize crop to 13.97 million tonnes from a previous target of 13.78 million and 12.74 million produced in 1995.
